Quote verbatim in current Isentress label (Revised 5/2022), rabbit sentence. Note overstates slightly: the rat study showed increased supernumerary ribs at 600 mg/kg/day; say 'no malformations' rather than 'no adverse developmental outcomes'.

Zash 2019 quote verbatim (and open access, PMC6995896, so not abstract-only). But the comparison was published in 2018: Zash 2018 letter is quotable (PMC6550482: '4 (0.94%) had a neural-tube defect' among 426), and the Tivicay label revised 09/2018 (accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2018/204790s016s018lbl.pdf) puts 'No adverse effects on embryo-fetal (rats and rabbits) ... development were observed at up to the highest dose tested' beside the 0.94% vs 0.12% human data in 8.1 -> primary source that makes the comparison, comparison_stated=true, year 2018. Animal side is also quotable from the 2013 FDA pharm review (204790Orig1s000PharmR.pdf): 'oral administration of DTG to pregnant rats and rabbits did not result in teratogenicity at systemic exposures up to 27X the human exposure for a 50 mg BID dose.' Contra as of 2018 stands under rule 5; the later attenuation is a new entry (see missing, rule_questions[1]).

rule_questions: Dose/efficacy registry dates: Protocol 004 is NCT00100048 (results first posted 2010-03-29); the draft left registry_date null after not locating it. No rule issue, listed here so the fact fields are filled.

A contradiction that later resolved: the 2018 published comparison (animal EFD negative vs 0.94% human NTD) was a contradiction when published; by 2025 the human estimate is 0.10% vs 0.11% and the animal prediction turned out right. Rule 5 forbids using later knowledge to re-score 2018, and 'one entry per change of status' implies a later entry, but the status table has no state for 'contradiction withdrawn' and 'contra overrides every matched status' could be read as permanent. Proposed reading: keep contra at 2018 and add a later 'same' entry dated to the year the attenuated comparison was published (2025 peer-reviewed, or the first label revision that said 'did not differ significantly'). Needs a house decision.

Engagement via resistance mapping: Cooper 2008 says patient mutations were 'known to be associated with phenotypic resistance' (a cell-culture measurement), which I read as the primary source itself stating model-patient concordance, so comparison_stated should be true and 'same' holds. If the house requires an explicit side-by-side model-vs-patient statement, the entry drops to untested, not contra. Also undecided by the brief: whether resistance-mutation concordance counts as 'hits its target in patients' for antivirals, where no occupancy readout exists.

Year when a label revision publishes the comparison before the peer-reviewed paper: the 09/2018 Tivicay label is the first primary source that juxtaposes animal and human data; the brief's 'year = print_year' convention does not say whether a label revision date counts as the publication year. I used 2018 either way (the Zash 2018 letter is also quotable).
